scope: Exact classical cosmological linear response; finite smooth SO(3)-invariant first-derivative P(phi,B) scalar actions, positive full K and Fourier C_n, regular unconstrained evolution, fixed physical known-matter metric and normalization.

claims.statement: mu_T=C_z(b_x,b_x); Pi=2 i p C_z(b_x,w_x); |Pi|^2<=4 p^2 mu_T C_z(w_x*,w_x), for arbitrary finite species and cross-couplings.
claims.critical_hypothesis: Full Fourier C_z is positive semidefinite; no claim of pointwise positivity of the entire C_ij gradient block.

claims.statement: Zero action-conjugate tensor response forces M=F=E=0 through contact -(M+F K^-1 F^T) and regular slope E K^-1 E^T.
claims.critical_hypothesis: Exact full sourced retarded Green equality, regular finite K>0, M>=0 and no metric derivatives.

claims.statement: Every admitted finite scalar multiplet theory with exactly GR-normalized full retarded tensor response has zero dark scalar anisotropic stress for all scalar solutions and initial modes.
f(R)=R-6H^2+R^2/(12H^2) at R=12H^2 has F=3, scalar mass squared 2H^2, matched full tensors at M^2=3M0^2, and an exact conserved-dust scalar response violating the class invariant.
claims.physical_source: Positive weak initial dust on a finite Cauchy domain, separately conserved at first order; no source creation step.
claims.initial_conditions: Specific phase ratios use zero scalar data. Initial-independent relation (d_tau^2+k^2)[a(Phi-Psi)]=-(k^2/3)a(Phi+Psi) holds for arbitrary scalar data.

claims.statement: At phase pi/2 the zero-initial target has eta=1/2 and force/lensing ratio 4/3; at phase pi it has eta=1/5 and force/lensing ratio 5/3. The admitted exactly GR-tensor class requires both ratios 1 when known scalar anisotropic stress vanishes.
claims.empirical_input: None supplied. Full tensor calibration and potential reconstruction are separate experimental inputs.

claims.statement: Single-solid/supersolid slip-tensor mass relations and f(R) scalar effects are known. Priority of the arbitrary-multiplet extension, broader local-action coverage and finite-error empirical exclusion remain unresolved.
